subject: FY2026 Preliminary Budget Review
overview: The Committee of the Whole conducted its third preliminary budget meeting for fiscal year 2026, reviewing the proposed budgets and operational priorities for six municipal departments. Discussions centered on the transition of grant-funded positions to the general fund, infrastructure improvements, and the city's long-term fiscal stability.

items.title: Board of Health and Civil Defense
items.summary: Discussed the transition of two ARPA-funded positions to the general fund and highlights from regional public health grants. The committee requested data from the Police Department regarding the volume of animal control calls handled by officers outside of regular business hours.

items.title: Facilities Department
items.summary: Reviewed utility cost increases driven by natural gas prices and updates on City Hall restoration projects including LED lighting and window repairs. Director Paul Righi provided a preliminary estimate of under $100,000 for chamber renovations should the council expand to 11 members.

items.title: Information Technology
items.summary: Presented updates on capital projects including the City Hall network recabling, a new fire department alerting system, and the replacement of the city's phone system. The department is prioritizing digital transformation to move more permitting and billing processes online.

items.title: Elections Department
items.summary: Announced that a new elections manager would begin work in May to oversee the upcoming municipal election. The budget reflects an increase for ballot printing costs, which are a local responsibility for municipal-only cycles.

items.title: Law Department
items.summary: Introduced new City Solicitor Kevin Foley and discussed the transition from reliance on outside counsel to in-house management. The committee debated the necessity of hiring an assistant city solicitor to handle the high volume of public records requests and legislative drafting.

items.title: Fiscal Policy and Free Cash Debate
items.summary: Councilors and the administration engaged in an extended debate regarding the city's $28 million free cash balance and the use of one-time ARPA funds. Discussion focused on whether high reserves indicate fiscal mismanagement or a necessary cushion against future structural deficits and debt requirements for major capital projects.

items.title: Executive Department
items.summary: Reviewed the Mayor’s Office budget, which includes the removal of a special projects coordinator in favor of internship funding and a shift in communications staffing. The committee requested an update on the current activity and membership status of the Medford Arts Council.
